about: Ai4Qi audit library. Audits are real where a source is given. Topic judgements are written by Claude from the detailed audits and should be checked by a consultant.

topic_knowledge.topic: Supracondylar fracture nerve and vessel documentation
topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Under half fully documented; anterior interosseous nerve worst, as low as 10%
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: A proforma, ideally electronic and built into clerking. Compliance rises to 70–95%.
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Teaching alone; gains fade when the proforma isn't used
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Done at least seven times with the same finding and fix. Don't repeat it. Audit whether the proforma is still used a year on, or audit documentation after manipulation, which nobody measures.
topic_knowledge.evidence: Detailed records in this library; judgement written by Claude from them

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Several Royal College items recorded in under 10% of notes; post-op plan and tourniquet time often poor
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Typed or electronic template. One unit went from 9.5% to 67% typed notes; post-op instructions from 40% to 92%.
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Templates don't fix items surgeons don't know: estimated blood loss stayed at 7–8%
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Heavily overdone. Only worth doing if your unit has no electronic template, or if you audit one item templates miss, such as blood loss or implant traceability.

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: About half delayed beyond 36 hours; mean around 49 hours; most delays organisational, not medical
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Structural change: extra morning trauma lists (41% to 78% within 36 h), a daytime emergency theatre (delays 49% to 26%), a seven-day consultant rota, or nurse-led vitamin K in ED (median 50 h to 34 h for warfarin patients)
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Teaching or reminders. No audit in the library improved timing without changing capacity or process.
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Your data already exists in the national hip fracture database. Don't recollect it. Pick one delay reason from your own data, such as anticoagulation or echo, and change the process behind it.
topic_knowledge.evidence: Detailed records in this library; judgement written by Claude from them

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Scoring systems almost never used: 0–2.6%. Imaging ranges from 61.3% to 92.5%. Surgery within 24 hours of decision 73.4–89.1%, delays mostly theatre capacity. Negative appendicectomy 4.2–15.4%. Postoperative antibiotics given to 67.2–92.1%, with choice and duration varying widely.
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Only one closed loop. Time to diagnosis fell from 16.8 to 8.27 hours, diagnosis to surgery from 28.1 to 20.54 hours, drains from 44% to 31%, postoperative antibiotics from 92.1% to 75.6% and complications from 17.8% to 3.3% [2853]. The intervention is not described.
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Scoring system use stayed low, 0% to 3.3% [2853]. No other re-audit reported; an educational push on scoring was only proposed [2255].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: A broad 'management of appendicitis' audit mostly re-finds low score use and theatre delays. Pick one measurable item and close the loop. Most useful: why CT- or ultrasound-diagnosed cases are histologically negative (about 25% in one unit [2839]) and whether postoperative antibiotics are really needed.
topic_knowledge.evidence: Detailed records in this library; judgement written by Claude from them

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Diagnosis within 48 hours is near-universal (97–100%). Severity scoring is poor: 6–38% documented. Ultrasound within 24 hours 25–41%. Cause identified in 55–82%, with up to 46% labelled idiopathic. Inappropriate antibiotics in 42% and 22 of 56. Index-admission or two-week cholecystectomy as low as 7.1–18%.
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: A weekly benign upper GI MDT with ERCP and hot cholecystectomy pathways: two-week cholecystectomy 75% to 100%, imaging within 24 hours 100%, escalation 0% to 60% [2602]. Extra hot chole slots: early cholecystectomy 18% to 31%, inappropriate antibiotics 42% to 28% [2704]. Teaching and MDT posters: aetiology 62% to 100%, risk stratification 38% to 65% [2881].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Risk stratification stayed below standard after teaching, at 65% [2881], and Glasgow score within 48 hours reached only 50% [2602]. Early cholecystectomy still only 31% after extra theatre slots [2704]. Most projects planned bundles, proformas or pathways but reported no re-audit [2084, 2471, 2572, 2879, 2880].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Heavily audited, and most projects never close the loop. Pick one measure, such as Glasgow-Imrie scoring at 48 hours or cholecystectomy within two weeks for gallstone cases, and re-audit it. Fluid volumes, nutrition and antibiotic indication are rarely measured and are worth doing.

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Severity score documented in a minority. 0/51 at one DGH [2801], 10% [2736], 16.7% [2857], 17% [2725], 33% [2444] and 44% [2548]. Scores that are done are often used wrongly, and high scores are rarely escalated (17% [2548]).
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: A score built into clerking. An electronic tick box took scoring from 44% to 84% and escalation of scores ≥3 from 17% to 100% [2548]. BISAP printed on the clerking proforma: 10% to 80% [2736]. Teaching plus an on-call process to score every new admission: 16.7% to 81.8% [2857].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Teaching, posters and an electronic template only reached 30% from 17% [2725]. Presentation, posters and email alone reached 66% before the tick box was added [2548]. An e-care proforma was used in 66.6%, but only 7/18 were fully completed [2801].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Every audit finds the same thing and the same fix. Only repeat it if your clerking has no built-in score. More useful: audit whether scores ≥3 are escalated in time, or whether CT is being requested without indication, which one unit found in almost half [2444].
topic_knowledge.evidence: Detailed records in this library; judgement written by Claude from them

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Six-monthly weight, pulse and blood pressure are the weak point, especially in adult CMHTs. Recording ranges from 8–19% [3222] to 57–84% [3286, 3646]; only 30.9% are monitored within NICE intervals [3646]. Some CAMHS and GP shared-care samples score 90–100% [3411, 3521, 3549]. Centiles are rarely used: BP 10%, HR 0% [3549].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: A dedicated ADHD clinic with a new initiation and shared-care process: annual BP 62.0% to 90.4%, weight 56.7% to 80.3%, longest wait 330 to 125 days (n=267 to 327) [3551]. A centralised caseload list and rating-scale retrieval: rating scales 3/7 to 6/7 [3506]. Presenting results raised weight 15% to 45%, HR 8% to 40%, BP 19% to 50% [3222].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Teaching and NICE posters did not move BP centiles (10% to 2%) or HR centiles (0% to 0%), because the electronic record cannot convert them [3549]. After presentation alone, Glasgow still missed NICE at 40–50% [3222]. In the clinic model, 6-monthly monitoring improved less than 12-monthly [3551].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Most audits here are single-cycle snapshots of the same obs. The only large gain came from reorganising the service, not from teaching. Audit 6-monthly monitoring after a system change, or whether prescribing continues despite non-attendance, rather than repeating a baseline.

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Freehand clerking misses much. Vital signs 25–46%, medications 20–48%, VTE plan 14–32%, social history 36–40%. Only 4% of surgical proformas fully completed at Ipswich. Psychiatry clerkings are similar: aggregate compliance 50.6%, risk management plan 8.6%.
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: A specialty proforma. ENT referral source 28% to 97%, VTE 14% to 78% [2048]. Galway items rose to 94–100% [1639]. Paediatric booklets gave 33% absolute gain, medications 48% to 99% [1581]. Complete clerking 36% to 88% [1226]. Psychiatry risk assessment 18% to 59% [3359]. A doctor's assistant raised consultant review within 14 h from 47% to 97% [2696].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Induction lecture alone: NEWS 46% to 54%, advice to patients 0% to 16% [2496]. Proformas leave gaps: vital signs stuck at 52–70% [1581][1639], investigation results 30% to 35% [1680]. Moving online cut 'time recorded' 18% to 0% [1209]. Full proforma completion only 4% to 26% [2301].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Heavily overdone, with the same finding and fix every time. Don't repeat it if a proforma exists. Audit whether the proforma is actually used, or the items proformas still miss: observations, investigation results and risk management plans.

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Withdrawal scoring is the weak point. CIWA within 24 hours was 1% [3627]; CIWA-Ar completed 23.97% [3575]; applied 44%, correctly scored 24% [3310]. Complete drinking history 4% [3310]. Physical examination is good at 84–98%, but cognitive assessment before discharge was 7% [3467]. Addiction specialist oversight on acute wards was 4% [3299].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: A ward SOP with risk profiling, nurse-administered CIWA-Ar, a symptom-triggered regimen and front-loading for high risk, after team training [3323]. At re-audit every patient had risk stratification recorded and all got the symptom-triggered regimen. Oral lorazepam fell from 3324 mg for 63 patients to 10 mg for 39 patients.
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Repeated re-audits at one trust barely moved: CIWA within 24 hours went 1%, then 4%, then 17%; referral to community alcohol services fell to 0% [3627]. Teaching, induction and electronic CIWA-Ar prompts gave better confidence but no figures [3575]. Relapse prevention and specialist referral stayed below 60% [3446].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Most of these are one-off audits finding the same low CIWA use; only one loop shows a clear gain. Don't just count CIWA scores again. Audit whether a symptom-triggered protocol is followed and changes benzodiazepine doses, or measure referral to community alcohol services and cognitive assessment before discharge, which stay near zero.

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Mechanism of injury is usually well documented (86–100%). Skin, neurovascular and post-reduction checks are weaker: national BOAST 12 compliance 41.7% with neurovascular documentation 40.7% [1599]; skin 54–71% [1617, 1659]. Malreduction after fixation runs at 25–33% [1569, 1582]. Early weight-bearing after surgery is rare (10% [1617]).
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Education with infographic posters cut malreduction from 25% to 9.4% [1582]. A process change backed by education cut malreduction from 33% to 2.4% [1569]. Induction and trauma-meeting teaching lifted precise documentation from 17% to 88% [1659]. Posters and specialist teaching raised saved syndesmosis stress images from 55% to 82% [1720]. A protocol cut inappropriate fracture clinic referrals by 53% [1448].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Education and reflection alone did not help: malreduction rose to 43.8% at interim re-audit [1569]. One interactive plaster session plus posters did not significantly improve cast angle (27.7% to 37.7% acceptable, p=0.231), with only 3% gain where junior doctors were trained [1668]. The 'DNVI' shorthand persisted after teaching [1659].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: ED documentation of BOAST standards is heavily audited and usually improves with teaching. More useful is measuring outcome: malreduction on post-operative films, syndesmosis testing, or early weight-bearing and its documented reasons. Full BOAST 12 compliance was linked to earlier discharge [1599], so a bundle measure is worth tracking.

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Overuse, not underuse. Cycle 1 finds antibiotics given in 50–88% of repairs, including low-risk ones. Guideline compliance runs 27–53%. High-risk mesh patients often get the wrong regimen: only 1 of 23 in one unit, 6 of 22 in another.
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Written high-risk criteria plus teaching cut antibiotic use from 87.8% to 48.1% with no rise in complications [2750]. Presenting results with posters raised compliance from 27.1% to 80% in ventral repair [2883] and to 84.6% in groin repair [2885], but re-audits covered one month and 13–15 patients.
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: No failed fix reported in these audits. Low-risk patients still got unneeded antibiotics after teaching: 2 of 4 [2883] and 1 of 2 [2885].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: A useful stewardship audit, but most units report the same overuse. Re-audit with enough patients and a longer period than one month. Measure the right drug and timing for high-risk mesh repairs, and record wound infection, as one audit did (1.04%) [2537].
topic_knowledge.evidence: Detailed records in this library; judgement written by Claude from them

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Pre-operative prophylaxis is nearly always given (85–100%). The problem is after the operation. 77.6–90.2% of uncomplicated cases still get post-operative antibiotics, and courses in complicated cases run long (mean 7.8–9.2 days). Correct agent or dose is often wrong: 2.2% trust-adherent agents in non-allergic patients [2363].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: A written post-operative antibiotic guideline: antibiotics withheld in uncomplicated cases rose from 54.3% to 78.3%, and stay fell from 23.3 to 14.5 hours [2851]. Posters, local guideline and an operation note proforma: omission in simple appendicitis 79% to 97%, correct 3–5 day course 12.1% to 61% [2770]. Teaching with the gentamicin calculator: 68.8% to 93.8% [2060].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Presenting results at forum and governance plus a theatre poster: uncomplicated cases on antibiotics only fell from 90.2% to 84.4% [2767]. Consultant teaching and an electronic theatre note: duration in complicated cases only 9.2 to 8.4 days [2868]. Course length in complicated appendicitis stayed inconsistent, 20% in a later cycle [2770].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Pre-operative prophylaxis is not worth auditing again; it is almost always given. Audit post-operative antibiotics in uncomplicated appendicitis and course length in complicated cases. Pair it with a written stopping rule in the operation note, and measure length of stay, which one audit showed can fall by 9 hours.
topic_knowledge.evidence: Detailed records in this library; judgement written by Claude from them

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Burden is often scored but rarely acted on. 75.4% of patients with ACB 3 or more had no documented intervention [3560]; 24% with ACB over 3 had no assessment [3452]; no patient needing review had one [3495]. Side effects mentioned in 7.5% and cognition monitored in 44.5% in learning disability teams [3658].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: No fix with measured improvement at re-audit is reported. Only one loop was closed [3412], and it got worse.
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Unimplemented recommendations from a first audit: patients scoring 0 at 4 weeks fell from roughly 50% to 13%, and more patients had a rising AEC score [3412]. Documented interventions had also declined against earlier local audits [3560].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: The gap is known: scores are calculated but nothing changes. Don't just measure the score again. Build AEC or ACB into the ward-round template or e-prescribing and audit whether a medication change follows a high score.
topic_knowledge.evidence: Detailed records in this library; judgement written by Claude from them

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Guideline-compliant prescribing in 35–76%. Indication and duration documented in 55.88–89%; review or stop dates as low as 17%. In one surgical clinic 71% of renal stone patients got antibiotics they did not need [1992]. Prophylactic prescriptions had no indication or duration recorded [1920].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Weekly microbiology-led ward rounds plus teaching: Microguide compliance 53% to 83% [1896]. Adding electronic prescribing that forces fields: review/stop dates 17% to 100%, indications 78% to 96%, IV duration 63% to 93% [1995]. QR-code posters and teaching: initial choice 59% to 82% [2780].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Posters and a talk gave modest gains: adherence 65% to 72% [1923]. In urology, discharge choice stayed at 61% and composite compliance only 43% to 53%, with 48% unjustified deviations [2780]. One unit reported improvement with no figures [2230].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Commonly done and the fix is known: a prompt in the prescribing system plus microbiology on the ward. Don't just measure documentation of indication. Audit appropriateness of discharge antibiotics, prophylactic courses, or antibiotics in conditions where none are needed, such as renal colic.

topic_knowledge.topic: Antipsychotic physical health monitoring in children and young people
topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Baseline bloods vary widely: 92% in one clinic and inpatients, 38% in community. Ongoing monitoring is poor: complete monitoring bloods 33%, full baseline 0%, six-monthly measures 16–20%, waist circumference 0%. Movement disorder assessment 0–54%. Samples are tiny, 7–26 patients.
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: A spreadsheet to track antipsychotic prescriptions: blood-test monitoring 17% to 100%, medication information 50% to 67%, but only 3 patients at re-audit [3413].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Recording in clinic letters with the schedule at the front of notes changed little: complete bloods 33% to 44%, baseline ECG 75% to 67%, current schedule 42% to 38%, 0% on PARIS [3169]. The unlicensed-indication protocol fell from 13% to 0% [3413].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Every audit finds the same gaps, in samples too small to show change. Audit who owns the monitoring when bloods and ECGs are sent to GPs, as results are hard to track. Pooling data across teams would give numbers large enough to re-audit.
topic_knowledge.evidence: Detailed records in this library; judgement written by Claude from them

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Basic bloods and BP often 70–90%. ECG, prolactin and waist circumference are poor, waist often 0% [3356][3690]. Full monitoring is rare: 0% [3150], 15.15% [3502], 18% [3689], 32% [3304]. Abnormal results are often not acted on: 27 of 32 with dyslipidaemia had no intervention [3211].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: A dedicated pathway or clinic. Junior-led virtual clinic with a phlebotomy/ECG pathway: per-patient compliance 9% to 69% [3257]. Weekly mop-up of outstanding results: 140 outstanding bloods to 24, then 100% by eight weeks [3417]. Screening tool plus GP coordination: 15.15% to 66.67% [3502]. Checklist and education: 29% to 68% [3690]. Ward round template and poster: side-effect monitoring 46.66% to 100% [3499].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Recommendations alone in general practice: three or more risk factors monitored rose only from 48% to 60%, and no measure reached 80% [3631]. During COVID 8/10 standards fell [3108]. Repeat ECG stayed below target at 79.17% [3499]. Clinic non-attendance stayed high: DNA 52% to 42% [3426], and 51% attended an on-site clinic [3262].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Heavily overdone: 39 audits, mostly single cycles with no re-audit, all finding the same gaps. Don't do another measurement audit. Audit whether abnormal results lead to action, such as statins or smoking cessation, or test a dedicated clinic or weekly results mop-up and re-audit it.
topic_knowledge.evidence: Detailed records in this library; judgement written by Claude from them

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Assessment of causes and target symptoms is good (88–100%) [3130, 3320, 3633, 3684]. Monitoring and review are poor: baseline ECG 50–54% [3320, 3431], reduction plan 8% [3431], discontinuation trial 33% [3320], physical monitoring at one year under 22% [3320]. Non-drug measures first in 42–76% [3320, 3339]. Trust monitoring form completed in 0% [3633].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: No re-audit reported in these audits. All seven are single-cycle.
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: No failed fix reported in these audits
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Seven audits, no closed loop. The baseline is known: good at documenting why, poor at ECG, bloods, and planned reduction. Pick one fix, such as a register or a due-date flag, and re-audit review and deprescribing at 6 weeks and 12 weeks.
topic_knowledge.evidence: Detailed records in this library; judgement written by Claude from them

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Formal scales are rarely used. GASS completion 5–27%, 7% on inpatient wards [3408]. AIMS in 9.1% of long-term antipsychotic patients [3124]. Side effects are noted informally in 96% of notes, but with no scale [3315].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: A new pharmacy team and guideline awareness raised six-monthly GASS from 5% to 75% [3620]. Sharing findings and recording scores on depot charts and SystmOne took GASS from 26.6% to 55.17% [3332].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Ward QI presentations and an infographic moved inpatient GASS only from 7% to 26% [3408]. Rating scale use rose only from 0% to 24% [3315]. Yearly GASS fell from 88% to 53% on the fourth re-audit when face-to-face reviews stopped [3702].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Commonly audited and the baseline is always poor. Gains depend on someone owning the task, such as pharmacy or depot clinics. More useful to audit whether an abnormal score led to a change in treatment, or tardive dyskinesia screening, which is rarely measured.
topic_knowledge.evidence: Detailed records in this library; judgement written by Claude from them

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Review and stop plans are the gap. PRN benzodiazepines reviewed within a week in 12/38, half continued over 3 weeks [3459]. Weekly review 0–6% [3644]. Zopiclone within 4 weeks in 27% [3567]. Discharge hypnotic review or stop plan 0% [3516]. Sleep hygiene advice 12.5–36.6%, CBT-I 0% [3296][3695]. Written advice 10.7% [3230].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Teaching residents at rotation start: PRN on discharge 15% to 0%, all with indication and reducing regimen documented [3561]. Unspecified changes cut zopiclone within 4 weeks from 27% to 83.3% [3567]. Acting on earlier recommendations raised discharge medication review from 0% to 56.25% (66.6% on the original wards) [3516]. Community indication documented 61.65% to 80.8% [3230].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Written advice fell from 10.7% to 5.8% across repeated cycles [3230]. Specific discontinuation plans reached only 18.75% [3516]. After the zopiclone fix, stop dates, indications and non-drug measures stayed poorly documented [3567]. Sleep teaching showed gains only on clinician self-report, with no record re-audit [3580].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Plenty of baseline audits, few with hard re-audit numbers. The consistent failures are weekly review of PRN and a written stop plan at discharge. Audit those, and whether non-drug insomnia care is actually offered, rather than prescribing rates alone.

topic_knowledge.topic: Best medical therapy in peripheral arterial disease
topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Antiplatelet use is often high but not universal (38.9–100%). High-dose statin optimisation is poor: 28% [2199], 29% [2533]. Lipid profiles are rarely checked (2.9–12.4%) [2753, 2823], HbA1c in 17.7–28.6%, and smoking cessation is documented in 13.9–40.5% [2753, 2465, 2038].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Teaching plus a ward-round computer raised smoking cessation advice from 19% to 100% [2038]. An admission document prompting antiplatelet and statin review raised BMT on discharge from 40% to 80% [2199]. MDT education raised atorvastatin 80mg optimisation from 29% to 64% [2533]. Teaching and posters raised lipid profiles from 12.4% to 65.0% and gastroprotection from 35.3% to 66.7% [2823].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: After teaching and posters, statin use stayed at 80% and HbA1c checks reached only 30.0% [2823]. After education and a handover proforma, 13% were still discharged on no secondary prevention (15% before), and statin initiation reached only 41% [2488]. BMT on admission stayed low (25%) [2199].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Many vascular units audit BMT and most find the same gaps. A prompt built into the admission or handover document does better than teaching alone. More useful would be tracking high-intensity statin dose, smoking cessation referral and whether primary care continues therapy after discharge.

topic_knowledge.topic: Blood transfusion and cross-matching in arthroplasty
topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Too much blood is cross-matched and too much transfused. C:T ratios run from 3.21 in hip replacement to 16.6:1 in spine surgery. MSBOS compliance was 52% in one spinal unit. Of transfused hip patients, 24–46% were inappropriate. Transfusions often go unrecorded (26%) and blood loss is recorded in only 57%.
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Stopping routine cross-match for THR with a day 2 blood count: unused units fell 96%, C:T 3.21 to 1.62 [1434]. A revised spinal guideline aligned with MSBOS: compliance 52% to 72%, over-cross-matching 43% to 12% [1763]. An agreed cross-match tariff cut units from 664 to 58, though C:T only moved from 16.6 to 11.5 [1436].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Staff education and policy amendments after 27% of THR patients were transfused (46% inappropriate): no reduction in transfusion rates [1479]. Several audits proposed ordering schedules but never re-audited [1413] [1495].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Cross-matching audits are done often and the fix is known: group and save, not cross-match. The harder question is who gets transfused and why. Audit transfusion triggers, single-unit transfusion and pre-operative anaemia; 57% of patients with Hb below 12 g/dl were transfused [1454].

topic_knowledge.topic: Bone health assessment in older people
topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Assessment is rarely done. FRAX was calculated in 0% [1179] and 33.3% [1182] of eligible inpatients. Only 25% were managed to NOGG 2021 [1160], and 37% of high-risk care home residents were on bone protection [1175]. Vitamin D and calcium are checked more often than FRAX. Bone treatment is started in few (6.7% [1179]).
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Putting FRAX and a management plan into a comprehensive geriatric assessment by a care home team: 100% of 183 residents assessed, and appropriate bone protection rose from 37% to 85% [1175]. One home went from 0% to 83%.
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: A bone health section on a Parkinson's clinic proforma: at re-audit 50% still needed intervention and DXA stayed at 33% (27% before) [1161]. Several audits only planned a fix and never re-audited [1179, 1182].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Everyone already knows FRAX is rarely done. A proforma alone is not enough; the one clear gain came when a named team did the assessment [1175]. Re-audit after the fix, and measure whether treatment was started and taken, not just whether FRAX was written down.

topic_knowledge.topic: Bone protection and secondary fracture prevention
topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Most fragility fracture patients leave without treatment started. Bone protection prescribed in 1.3–16% of hip fractures [1615][1693][1414]; 15.2% started after GP letters [1172]; 0% FRAX in falls [1146][1364]. Non-hip fractures fare worse: osteoporosis assessed in 25.7% vs 100% hip [1345]. GPs often do not act: 87% not started after discharge [1693].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Giving a named team responsibility: 13.9% to 100% assessed, sustained [1615]. Community fracture liaison nurse: 47.9% to 84.0% treated [1516]. Ward-round prompts: FRAX 0% to 86% [1146], 50% to 88% [1362]. Kardex stickers: 50.9% to 84.6% [1470]. Stickers, whiteboards and pathways: zoledronic acid 12.12% to 95.45% [1173].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Teaching, protocols, MDTs and a new clinic: bisphosphonates stayed poor (64% not given) and FRAX fell 54% to 18% [1693]. Rewritten GP letter: 40% to 51% [1346]. EHR referral alert: 5% to 19% [1637]. Awareness: 5/38 to 23/43 referred [1444]. PTH not measured after intervention [1598].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Heavily overdone in hip fracture, and relying on the GP letter fails. Audit non-hip fragility fractures, whether the first dose is given before discharge, or 12-month adherence (11.6% [1764]). Falls and exercise referral is also rarely measured [1177][1458].

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Most units miss the BSG two-week target. Timely cholecystectomy 6.6–32.6%, rising to 71% in one unit; inpatient Lap-C as low as 2%. Mean waits of 64 days to 11.2 weeks. Readmissions while waiting are common: 6 of 21 [2391], 32% [2774]. No documented reason for delay in 34.8% [2578].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Structural change works. A consultant-led biliary service with live tracking and inpatient Lap-C: two-week Lap-C 27% to 69–79%, time to Lap-C 68 to 13 days [2342, 2422]. Expedited pathway and tracker: timely 15.2% to 43% [2774]. P2 listing and cancelling elective work: 71% to 86% [2745]. Re-audit 32.6% to 64.5% [2589].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: COVID elective backlog took one unit from full compliance to 0 of 4 [2208]. Even after change, only half were operated [2774], and barriers persisted: ultrasound slots, hot lists and reluctance to operate acutely [2589]. Length of stay for index surgery rose from 3 to 6 days [2745].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Heavily audited; every unit finds the same gap. Another baseline adds nothing. If you do it, audit the delay by step (fitness, MRCP, ERCP, theatre) and readmissions while waiting, and track whether a hot-list or tracker survives beyond a year.

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Diagnosis and current medication are nearly always recorded (80–100%). Allergies (13–27.5%), user-friendly information or useful links (7.5–23%), copying in service users (3%), crisis planning (20%) and actions for the GP are the weak items. Timeliness is usually good: letters within 7 days 92–99%, within 14 days 95%.
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: A letter template with recommended headings plus junior teaching: psychiatric diagnosis 83.5% to 97.1%, follow-up plan 80.2% to 98.6%, care coordinator 8.3% to 54.3% [3298]. At re-audit in one CAMHS clinic, medication indications rose 32.5% to 56.6% and risk assessment 70% to 86.6% [3270].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: After the template, action for GP fell from 44.6% to 27.1% and medical comorbidity stayed low, 31.4% to 28.6% [3298]; the template often went unused. Allergies fell from 27.5% to 3.3% and useful links stayed at 13.3% [3270].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Letters score well on diagnosis, medication and timeliness, so don't re-audit those. Measure what the GP needs: a clear action for the GP, allergies and physical health. Then check whether the template is actually used.

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Around half of items met. CRAMS criteria met in 52.9% of entries [3461]. Emergency bleep documentation 44% [3355]. Most ward review questions below 80%; responsible clinician recorded in 23.3% [3301]. Personal care in nursing notes 17% [3140]. Resuscitation status 39% and capacity 14% [3249].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Automating or embedding fields. Auto-filled responsible clinician rose from 23.3% to 99.5% [3301]. An electronic bleep checklist took documentation from 44% to 90% [3355]. A note format emailed with one-to-one follow-up took personal care from 17% to 89% [3140]. Discussion at daily huddles raised CRAMS compliance from 52.9% to 71.6% [3461].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Non-automated measures (teaching, posters) had limited effect; 17 questions stayed low [3301]. Resuscitation status stayed at 40–50% despite an electronic checklist [3249]. Medical ward doctor documentation only reached 57% [3355]. Many entries still missed full CRAMS criteria [3461].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Generic note audits find the same thing and are hard to act on. Pick one item that matters and is missing, such as resuscitation status or capacity, and fix it in the electronic record. Mandatory or auto-completed fields beat teaching.

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: FBC is near 100% [3250, 3410, 3489]. Lipids are usually checked (81–92%) [3113, 3402], but cardiovascular risk is not: QRISK3 0% [3113], risk score 3.70% [3402]. Lipids sent to GP 18.18% [3402]. Older adults: glucose, prolactin and lipids 0% [3410]. Initiation: no routine troponin, baseline ECG 80% [3700]; pre-treatment troponin 14%, CRP 0% [3489].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: 20-minute nurse training on three days plus an aide-memoire: inappropriate clozapine tests fell from 53% to none, with routine FBCs for all [3432]. A ward already using a monitoring checklist achieved 100% adherence [3276].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: No failed fix reported in these audits
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: FBC monitoring is safe and not worth auditing again. The gaps are cardiovascular risk scoring, sending results to the GP, and troponin and CRP during initiation. Most audits here never re-audited, so close the loop on one of those.

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Levels are taken irregularly and often at the wrong time. Mean interval 10 months 2 weeks, 32% above range [3114]. Only 12.9–56.3% of samples taken over 15 hours post dose [3279]. Levels rechecked after smoking change in 42.86% [3385]. Toxicity screening for levels >600 in 67% [3389].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: No audit in these records reports a re-audit. None can be cited as working.
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: No failed fix reported in these audits
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: All five audits are single cycles, so a closed loop would add something. Pick one specific trigger, such as a change in smoking status or a high level, and audit the response. Sample timing with bespoke dosing regimes is poorly covered by guidance and worth measuring.
topic_knowledge.evidence: Detailed records in this library; judgement written by Claude from them

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Generic risks are almost always written; specific ones are not. Bleeding and infection near 100%, but mortality 13.2–49.2%, dislocation 0% and leg length 0% [1584][1656][2738]. Abbreviations in 54% of orthopaedic forms and 99% of surgical forms [1614][2544]. Copy offered to patients 0–12% [2613][2711][1586]. COVID-19 risk recorded 41–59% [1231][1237][2105]. Capacity documented 11.6–13.9% in arthroplasty [1257].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Pre-printed or procedure-specific forms: all risks 100% [1553][2739]; risks per form 56.6% to 87.9% with stickers [1695]; uptake 91% [2008]. Electronic auto-filled forms improved most items [2317]. Emails, stickers and posters cut abbreviations 54% to 22% [1614][1395]. Teaching and posters raised copies offered 0% to 74% [2711] and next-of-kin documentation 36% to 83% [1243].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Montgomery changed nothing: 53% vs 59% of risks [2008]. Posters and induction left mortality at 21% and leg length at 6% after three cycles [1584]. Written information stayed 8–14% [1606]. Elective COVID documentation stayed poor at 48.9% [1231]. Stickers ran out and copies offered fell to 8% [1586]. New risks absent from clinic letters rose to 79% [2419].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Heavily overdone, 45 audits, especially hip fracture, abbreviations and COVID risk. Teaching gives partial gains; procedure-specific or electronic forms reach near 100%. Don't audit the form again. Audit whether consent starts in clinic rather than on the day [2713][2528], whether patients get a copy and leaflet, and whether they understand the risks.
topic_knowledge.evidence: Detailed records in this library; judgement written by Claude from them

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Most core surgical trainees miss training standards. Nationally, 25.5% met the theatre standard and 5% met both standards [1547]. Only 25% of rotas met the standard, with a mean deficit of 18.5 sessions per 6 months [2125]. Regionally, 45% had consistent theatre access and 19% scheduled clinic time [2682].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Presenting results to the trainee committee and trust leadership, with rota redesign, raised theatre access from 45% to 78% and clinic time from 19% to 50% [2682]. Rostering Advanced Clinical Practitioners onto trauma wards cut locum ward cover from 36.6% to 23.7% and saved £8,140 over three weeks [1229].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Over 75% of trainees still could not attend mandatory teaching after rota changes, and a later cycle fell back to 68% theatre and 39% clinic, with three trusts showing no progress [2682]. Protected theatre time stayed below 1 day/week despite ACP cover [1229].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Surveys of trainee exposure are common and consistently show the same shortfall. The value lies in rota-level data that managers can act on, not questionnaires with low response rates. Measure protected theatre and clinic sessions actually worked, and teaching attendance, across repeated cycles.

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Day-case rates of 45–74% against targets of 60%, 75% or 90%. A third of overnight stays have no clinical reason (34–39%). Common causes are pain, nausea, monitoring, drains and afternoon operating. No surgeon recorded pneumoperitoneum pressure in one unit.
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Adapting GIRFT advice into trust guidelines raised the day-case rate from 45% to 70%, and 77.8% at a second site [2625]. Extending day unit recovery to 9pm plus liver bed local anaesthetic raised it from 64% to 73% [2684].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: No failed fix reported in these audits. Even after re-audit, rates stayed below the 90% GIRFT target, and 14-day readmission was 9% [2625].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: A common audit, and the causes are now well known. Only worth doing if you change something concrete: recovery hours, morning slots for older or high-BMI patients, no drains. Check coding first; hot list cases skewed one unit's GIRFT figure [2588]. Also measure readmission, not just same-day discharge.
topic_knowledge.evidence: Detailed records in this library; judgement written by Claude from them

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Screening with the 4AT or CAM is usually poor: 0–34% in most wards, as low as 2.7% [1829] and 3% [1870]. Delirium is common (14.5–50.7%) but rarely named in the notes (8.5–19%). Care plans and PINCH-ME risk factor work are documented in 8.5–28%. Antipsychotics are started without a diagnosis [1893].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Changes built into the notes work best. Electronic notes with a compulsory screen and switch to 4AT: 3% to 87% [1870]. A champions group plus proforma with 4AT sticker: 0% to 92% [1813]. A co-designed admission proforma: 53% to 79% [1899]. Bedside CAM-ICU training cut misdiagnosed 'psychosis' from 63% to 31% [1365].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Education, stickers and reminder emails: 4AT hit 100% in week 3 then fell to 1.3% by week 6 [1804]. Teaching alone: 25% to 35% [1153]. Lanyard cards: 9.5% to 43% [1898]; 7.5% to 40.6% [3466]. A bedside tool: 34% to 44% [1917]. Gains fell back between PDSA cycles [1846]. Formal diagnosis and management stayed low.
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Heavily overdone, with 17 audits and the same poor screening rate. Don't repeat a screening count. Only a compulsory electronic field or a proforma held gains. More useful: whether a positive 4AT leads to a diagnosis and a PINCH-ME plan, and antipsychotic use without a diagnosis.
topic_knowledge.evidence: Detailed records in this library; judgement written by Claude from them

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Licensed indication and dose are usually right (100% [1802]). Reviews lag: side effect review 46% [1802]; psychiatrist review within a year 60% (28/47) [3392]. Prescription-writing standards poor, 19% for interval wording [3223]. Overseas, 100% polypharmacy and no baseline ECG [3526].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Shared care re-audit rose from 83% to 96% compliance, fix not reported [3322]. Standardised prompts for dose-reduction discussion cut procyclidine use from 39% to 18%, with 44% getting de-prescribing action [3554].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: A memory aid at the front of depot card folders: interval wording only 19% to 31%, and signed, dated, printed name fell from 75% to 15% because the card had no space for a name [3223].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Dose and indication are rarely wrong, so don't audit them again. Measure annual psychiatrist and side-effect review, or anticholinergic co-prescribing. Fix the depot card itself rather than adding reminders.
topic_knowledge.evidence: Detailed records in this library; judgement written by Claude from them

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Usually under half complete. Overall compliance 8–55%; 'ideal' summaries 0–20%. Auto-filled fields reach 100%, but future plans, medication changes, allergy status, investigations and safety netting are poor. Psychiatry adds missing risk and crisis contacts. Timeliness is often weak: mean delays 12.7–14.6 days, 19.5% of forensic documents done.
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Mandatory electronic fields or templates: imaging results 0% to 92.9% [1337]; electronic versus handwritten, most items to 95–100% [1647]. Teaching: 55% to 91% adequate [2333], failure 60% to 15% [2212]. Checklist and feedback: follow-up plan 15.6% to 90.0% [1748]. Named doctor plus tracker: 19.5% to 81.5% [3675]. Nurse-sent protocol: 2/89 to 55% [3141].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Gains fade when feedback stops: 40% to 20% [1806]; 100% tapering to 85% [3147]. Poster-only feedback left most domains short [2462]. Safety netting fell 96.9% to 76.2% [1748] and stayed lowest at 32% [2884]. Diagnosis accuracy 68% to 72% [2087]. All SIGN criteria 0% to 6% [2490]. Delays worsened, 14.6 to 19.4 days [2651].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: One of the most over-audited topics, with the same finding each time. Don't do another completeness audit. Build the missing item into the electronic template, then audit whether it persists after the rotation changes, or audit accuracy of medication changes and safety-netting, which templates do not fix.

topic_knowledge.topic: Distal radius fracture time to surgery
topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Extra-articular fractures mostly meet the 7-day target (82–100%). Intra-articular fractures within 72 hours range from 4.3% to 65%. Hand trauma audits in this group show 46–86% within BSSH timeframes. Theatre capacity is the usual cause of delay: 73.7% of delays in one audit [1740] and 52% in another [1726].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Hand trauma timeliness met the project target, overall compliance 73% to 83%, bites 100% [1726]. Referral-based intra-articular timing rose 74% to 88% after education and a trauma list dropdown [1735].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Education and a dropdown did not hold: intra-articular within 3 days of injury 59% to 75% then 56%, extra-articular fell to 68% [1735]. Registrar email, teaching and a pathway left intra-articular compliance at 10% [1740]. Theatre efficiency recommendations: 74% to 72% [2518]. Flexor tendon surgery stayed at 86% [2205].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Teaching does not fix a theatre capacity problem, and these audits show it. Audit the pathway steps instead, with timestamps from injury to listing to surgery. The virtual fracture clinic route (0% compliant vs 37.5%) [1772] is the most useful thing to measure.
topic_knowledge.evidence: Detailed records in this library; judgement written by Claude from them

topic_knowledge.topic: DNACPR and ceilings of care documentation
topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Forms exist but are incomplete. None fully completed and 48% not endorsed by a consultant [1940]. 63.8% signed only by an NCHD [1915]. DNAR status in medical notes 35%, reasoning 32% [1873]. Discussion with patient often missing: 41% undocumented [1940]. Ceilings of care under 15% [1873].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Redesigning the form. Moving the treatment escalation plan to the front page of a new DNACPR form raised TEPs from 56% to 99% of patients not for CPR, with doctor's name and grade on every form [1839].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Two education sessions left DNAR status (35%) and reasoning (32%) unchanged. Relatives' discussion stayed at 48% and ceilings of care stayed under 15% [1873][1895]. After the redesign, 83.3% of patients still had no documented resuscitation status [1839].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Most of these audits are single-cycle, and teaching alone did not move the numbers. More useful: audit how many patients who need a decision have one at all, or add resuscitation and escalation status to the ward round proforma [3518]. Note [1873] and [1895] report the same audit.
topic_knowledge.evidence: Detailed records in this library; judgement written by Claude from them

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Driving status is recorded in a minority: 5% [3547], 17.7–18% [3369, 3396], 25% [3619, 3676], 29.1% [3541], 42% [3213]. Vehicle type is almost never asked (0–33%) [3231, 3396]. Advice at discharge is rarer still: 1 of 20 [3595], 5% [3228], 0–7% [3616]. Where drivers are identified, advice is often given (67%) [3396, 3619].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: A driving field in the assessment or ward round template, usually with prompts and teaching. Status 25% to 85% [3619]; 25% to 90.9% [3676]; advice 29.1% to 81.7% with MDT checklist and leaflets [3541]; 17.7% to 56.0% [3369]; median 60% to 83% [3552]. DVLA advice on discharge summaries 5% to 56% [3228].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Teaching and written guidance: 42% to 47% [3213]. Presenting results to the MDT: advice 0–7% to 21–27%, below the 50% target [3616]. Status can improve while advice lags: 50% status but advice 13.6% [3547]; advice varied weekly with no run chart shift [3552]. Insurer advice fell 45% to 0% [3443].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Heavily overdone, with the same low baseline and the same template fix. Do not audit whether status is recorded again. Audit whether confirmed drivers get specific advice and DVLA duty explained, or whether a template field is still used a year on.
topic_knowledge.evidence: Detailed records in this library; judgement written by Claude from them

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Consent forms are usually complete, but the rest is not. Outcome scales are patchy: MADRS 0–71.4%, baseline CGI 20% [3192][3384][3559]. Cognitive checks fall after the course: 56.9% [3464], under 75% by completion [3544]. No 3- or 6-month follow-up [3418]. Risk/benefit discussion 50% [3347]. Right to withdraw explained to none [3523].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Checklists, then an ECT discharge summary for every patient: legal status 5% to 100%, Mini-ACE 5% to 100%, MADRS 0% to 100% [3192].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: No failed fix reported in these audits
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Only one of nine audits closed the loop. Consent paperwork is usually fine, so don't audit that alone. Audit outcome and cognitive monitoring through and after the course, including 3- and 6-month follow-up, which is where every service falls down.
topic_knowledge.evidence: Detailed records in this library; judgement written by Claude from them

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: A NELA score is often calculated but rarely shared. Score recorded 21–39.6% at some sites [2427][2571], 80–94.7% at others [2162][2707]. Mortality risk on the consent form 17.86–40% [2707][2582]; discussion with patient or family documented 14% [2061]. Frailty assessed in 38.6% of over-65s [2571]; elderly care input 12.5% [2707].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Periodic reminders to surgeons at meetings plus posters, over three cycles [2582]. Mortality on the consent form rose from 40% to 71% to 92% (p < 0.0001).
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: In the same audit, documented discussion in the medical notes rose only from 35% to 51% [2582]. No other intervention was re-audited.
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Only one of six audits closed the loop; the rest are baselines with the same finding. The score gets done for NELA, not for the patient. Audit whether the risk is discussed and recorded in the notes, and whether frailty and elderly care input happen for older patients.
topic_knowledge.evidence: Detailed records in this library; judgement written by Claude from them

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Follow-up endoscopy is both late and misdirected. Only 23% were scoped within the 8-week target [2104], and 1 of 21 within 6–8 weeks [2798]. Many uncomplicated cases are scoped without need: 78.9% [2556], 42/55 without an indication [2772], 27 unnecessary cases [2892]. Yet 39% with an indication had no endoscopy [2772]. Hinchey score was recorded in 8.7% [2892].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Staff training and awareness raised timely colonoscopy in complicated cases from 5% to 46% [2798]. Targeted teaching and posters raised appropriate endoscopy booking from 60% to 71% [2836]. Without a stated intervention, flexible sigmoidoscopy in uncomplicated cases fell from 48.8% to 29.4% [2250].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: No intervention was followed by no improvement. Timeliness stayed poor: after staff training, only 6 of 18 complicated cases had timely colonoscopy [2798]. After teaching and posters, 29% of eligible patients still had no endoscopy booked [2836].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: The yield in uncomplicated disease is low: no cancer in 82 colonoscopies [2556], no malignancy in the over-investigated group [2892], and £35,202 spent on unindicated scopes [2772]. Audit whether complicated cases get timely scoping and whether uncomplicated cases are spared it. Record CT staging so the indication can be judged.
topic_knowledge.evidence: Detailed records in this library; judgement written by Claude from them

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Enhanced recovery is patchy. Only 36% of Scottish units had a programme and 35% of patients were catheterised. Day 0 or 24-hour mobilisation runs about 66%. Length of stay was 3.6 days in one unit; same-day hip discharge was 54.3% in another.
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: A multidisciplinary group with parallel PDSA cycles (local infiltration, preprinted charts, nurse-led mobilisation, ring-fenced ward) cut stay from 3.6 to 2.4 days for hips and 2.0 for knees [1605]. Feedback to the team: 24-hour mobilisation 66.0% to 90.5% [1749]. Spinal lidocaine: same-day discharge 54.3% to 80.6% [1753]. National steering: programmes 36% to 68%, catheterisation 35% to 26% [1484].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: No failed fix reported in these audits. Median stay did not change (2 days) despite better mobilisation [1749]. Physiotherapy stayed rare on day 0: none documented in one unit [1749] and 3.5% of first mobilisations in another [1605].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Measuring length of stay alone tells you little. Audit single elements that decide discharge: day 0 mobilisation, pain and nausea control, catheter use. Pain was the commonest barrier to discharge [1749]. Record 30-day readmissions and complications alongside, as same-day discharge audits did [1753].
topic_knowledge.evidence: Detailed records in this library; judgement written by Claude from them

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Overall compliance runs at about 64–70% [2130, 2385]. Pre-operative and intra-operative elements are usually done well. Post-operative elements lag: opioid avoidance only 7.9–8% [2130, 2376], nutritional drinks 0–44.3% [2701, 2376], and routine drains, NG tubes and bowel preparation persist. Mean stay 5.5–9.8 days at baseline.
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: An ERAS proforma: in notes 0% to 92%, anti-emetics 32% to 100%, stay 5.5 to 3.75 days [2501]. Overall adherence 63.9% to 81.1%, stay 9.8 to 7.1 days [2385]. A discharge checklist: median stay 5 to 4 days, day 1 catheter removal 63% to 80% [2656]. Nutritional work: supplements 0% to 75% [2701]. MDT protocol: regular medicines 37% to 62% [2773].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Opioids stayed at 100% after an action plan; drains (85%) and NG tubes (80%) remained high [2835]. Day 1 trial without catheter reached only 50% [2501]. Physiotherapy referral fell from 100% to 85% [2701].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Don't audit the whole ERAS bundle again; the pre-operative parts are fine. Pick one post-operative element that stays poor, such as opioid avoidance, drains or nutrition drinks, and link it to length of stay, which several audits showed can fall.
topic_knowledge.evidence: Detailed records in this library; judgement written by Claude from them

topic_knowledge.topic: Extended VTE prophylaxis after abdominal cancer surgery
topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Wide range. Older or unprotocolled units 14–32% compliance [2270][2583][2284]; others 61% [2231] to 82–84% [2505][2341]. Emergency cases worse: 55% vs 88% elective [2341]. After appendicectomy none had 7 days' prophylaxis [2251].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Unit or Trust protocol: 14% to 91% with protocol change and education [2270]; 14.1% to 86.3%, then 92.6% after a 28-day policy [2583]. An ERAS nurse: 32% to 74% [2284]. A ward poster: 82% to 90% [2505].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: A 14-day interim protocol only reached 26% compliance before the 28-day protocol [2270].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Well covered in elective cancer surgery once a protocol exists. More useful to audit emergency laparotomy patients, where compliance falls, or whether patients actually complete 28 days at home.
topic_knowledge.evidence: Detailed records in this library; judgement written by Claude from them

topic_knowledge.topic: Fracture clinic standards and virtual fracture clinic
topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Virtual fracture clinics generally meet the 72-hour review: mean 2.33 days [1249], 93.8% within 72 hours [1330]. Without one, 6% were seen in time [1538]. Referral quality is the weak point: 21% suitable for direct ED discharge [1222], 32.1% of ED upper limb referrals had errors [1777]. Advanced imaging waits reach 30 days.
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Introducing a VFC: 6% to 100% within 72 hours [1538]. Mandatory VFC triage and early discharge cut face-to-face appointments by 50.2% [1694]. Joint ED guidelines: inappropriate referrals 80 to 24 [1327], errors 32.1% to 12.6% [1777]. ED education: soft tissue referrals 15.1% to 4.5% [1367]. Radiology priority slots: imaging wait 4.51 to 3.56 days [1316].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Clinic logistics barely changed: appointment wait 3.55 to 3.21 days, waiting area still rated inadequate by 41.49% [1550]. Radial head fractures were still seen in clinic in 64% [1367]. Virtual discharge fell from 17.9% to 13.6% [1611].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: The 72-hour standard is usually met once a VFC exists, so auditing it again adds little. More useful: the quality of ED referrals, delays to advanced imaging, and patient safety or satisfaction after virtual discharge, which one large audit said was not assessed [1694].
topic_knowledge.evidence: Detailed records in this library; judgement written by Claude from them

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Clinical Frailty Scale is rarely recorded at first contact in emergency surgery: 0–8% in five audits, 28% in one. Two audits found frailty documented in 65% and 100%. Geriatric or frailty team input is near zero. When scored, 35–43% of older surgical patients are frail. Cognitive screening is poor (AMTS 7%, no cognitive note in 70%).
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Mandatory CFS in software plus poster and teaching: criterion 1 40% to 100% [2197]. Twice-weekly geriatric ward rounds: CFS 0 to 88% [2648]. EPR templates and education: CFS 0/47 to 50%, OPAL review 13% to 34% [2614]. Coloured forms and nurses flagging patients 70+: 0% to 88.2% [2502].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Teaching and a screening bundle: CFS 8% to 28%, MUST fell 82% to 67.3% [2784]. Teaching and a frailty section: 2.2% to 18.4% [2566]. Juniors' teaching: memory screen and AMTS fell [2211]. With CFS at 88%, only 18% of frail patients got geriatric input [2648].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Scoring frailty is well audited and the fix is known: make it mandatory in the clerking system. The gap is what happens next. Measure whether frail patients get geriatric review, cognitive screening and a DNACPR discussion.
topic_knowledge.evidence: Detailed records in this library; judgement written by Claude from them

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Poor adherence to European guidelines: 17% of pathways [2804], 36% [2184], 43.1% [2628]. Scans late: median 556 days to second scan [2372]. 41.6% lost to follow-up in primary care [2628]. Both over- and under-treatment: 58 unnecessary scans and 35 missed cholecystectomy referrals [2804].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Inviting overdue patients back. A GP practice sent invitations for repeat imaging or a consultation, and 100% returned to surveillance [2628].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: No failed fix reported in these audits
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Only one audit closed the loop, so a real re-audit would add something. Ultrasound reports are part of the problem: 0% documented sessility and 35% omitted wall thickness [2804]. Auditing radiology reports, or unnecessary cholecystectomy (true polyp in 6% [2590]), is more useful than another adherence count.
topic_knowledge.evidence: Detailed records in this library; judgement written by Claude from them

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Where a fast-track clinic exists, most are seen quickly: 70.8% by rheumatology within 24 hours [2913], all within 3 days [2957]. Outside a pathway it is poor: steroids 34%, rheumatology referral 55%, ultrasound 15% [2962]. Written information is patchy: 54% [2957], leaflets 43% of sites [2907]. Ophthalmology within 24 hours 50% with visual symptoms [2913].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: An SDEC pathway with a streamlined ultrasound order, teaching, posters and a probability score: ultrasound 15% to 77%, referral 55% to 77%, steroids 34% to 54% [2962]. Registrar hot clinics and more ultrasound capacity: referral to review 2.7 to 1.6 days, biopsy 41% to 7.5% [2922]. Regional feedback: pathways 2 to 6 sites, leaflets 43% to 80% [2907].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Time to rheumatology assessment did not change (1 to 1.5 days) [2962]. Steroid card provision did not change after regional feedback, and steroid taper protocols went from 8 to 7 sites [2907].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Speed of review is usually good where a clinic exists, so don't re-audit it there. The gaps are steroids started before referral, written information and bone protection. Audit the front door, such as ED or SDEC, where the pathway is often not used.

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Handover and ward round notes miss key items. RCS minimum dataset met in 31–45% [2486][2653][2788]. Outstanding tasks 6.2–38% [2093][1528]. Escalation plan 0%, drug monitoring 1% [2176]. Ward round VTE 0–26.5%, ceiling of care 1%, fluid balance 16% [2151][2785]. Trauma meetings documented in 64% [1709].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Structured templates, especially electronic. Weekend handover sticker: escalation plan 0% to 87%, diagnosis 21% to 96% [2176]. Ward round template: essential criteria 32% to 93%, VTE 70% to 98% [2526]. Handover list: outstanding tasks 6.2% to 80% [2093]. Electronic proforma: all but one criterion ≥95% [1528]. Trauma presentation template: complete 24.0% to 81.3% [1768].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Items without a template field stay poor: blood results 19% to 20% [1447], resuscitation status 7.0% to 9.2% [2378], whom to contact 0% to 14.70% [1634], TTO 12% to 5% [1556]. Teaching alone left diagnosis, VTE and antimicrobials unchanged [2677]. Induction tutorial plateaued at 50% completeness [2832]. Fluid balance worsened after a template [2525].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Very heavily overdone; forty audits, same result. Don't start another unless your unit has no template. Audit whether the template is still used after changeover, or target the items templates miss, such as resuscitation status, pending results and weekend handover.

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: HDAT is uncommon, 1.2–9% of patients [3343][3104][3190], but monitoring is poor. HDAT forms 0% [3190][3681], 1/378 [3596]. Monitoring compliance 26% [3615]. Quarterly bloods and ECG 8–23% [3138]; ECG after dose increase 36% [3104]; cardiovascular check before HDAT 41% [3373]. Prolactin and ECG are most often missed [3615].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Electronic flag and active therapy plan that orders tests and books appointments: monitoring 26% to 58%, flags and plans 100% [3615]. A local HDAT register with biannual review: average compliance 60.6% to 77%, HDAT form 0% to 67%, and HDAT stopped in 50% of the baseline cohort [3681]. Feedback to prescribers raised quarterly bloods to about 50–60% [3138].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: With no intervention, a second cycle got worse: exceeding BNF maxima 1% to 2.9%, polypharmacy 5.6% to 10.4%, HDAT forms 0.62% [3596]. After the register, blood tests and ECG fell by 25.4% and 75.1% relative [3681]. Quarterly ECG stayed about 40% [3138].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: The finding is always the same: forms and ECGs are missing. Only system fixes, a register or EHR flag, moved the numbers. More useful: audit whether HDAT is reviewed and stopped, since half the cohort came off after review [3681], and track ECG and prolactin specifically.

topic_knowledge.topic: Hip fracture analgesia and nerve block
topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Nerve block use is low and poorly documented: fascia iliaca block in 2.0% [1715], 24.5% [1612], 35% [1381] and 65% [1732]; documented within 2 h in 6.4% [1769]. Contraindications were documented in 0% without a block [1732]. Regular postoperative paracetamol 3 g/day was given to 16% [1679].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Teaching plus an enforced proforma with FICB sign-off raised block rate from 24.5% to 44.3% [1612]. Three PDSA cycles lifted block rate from 2.0% to 22.6% [1715]. Nurse-led audit and feedback raised postoperative paracetamol from 16% to 60% [1679]. An analgesia checklist cut time to first analgesia from 130 to 38.8 min and to FICB from 228 to 63.4 min [1732].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Practical sessions and a checklist did not raise FICB uptake (65% to 65%, p=0.74) or pain re-evaluation within 30 min (52.5% to 50%) [1732]. Preoperative paracetamol did not improve (9% to 16%, p=0.13) [1679]. The 50% block target was not met [1715].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: FICB rates are commonly audited. The better questions are time to block, documented reason when not given, and pain reassessment. Timing is often missing (43.2% of episodes with no block timing [1769]), so fix recording first with a mandatory timestamp.
topic_knowledge.evidence: Detailed records in this library; judgement written by Claude from them

topic_knowledge.topic: Hip fracture and registry data quality
topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Registry data are fairly complete but not accurate. Only 56% of hip fracture theatre forms were completed and 21% of those fully accurate. Elbow arthroplasty completeness was 63% (radial head 35%). Only 8–10% of records were error-free in one registry. Revisions go missing more than primaries. Coding errors run 50–69% of cases.
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Education plus a checklist sticker: form completion 56% to 81%, accuracy 21% to 56% [1370]. Trainee-led national record checks: elbow completeness 63% to 83%, accuracy 94% to 98% [1689]. An annual NJR audit cycle with named leads and missing-case statements: compliance 92.64% to 97.9% [1635]. A coding-friendly proforma: coding errors 50% to 5% [1657].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: No failed fix reported in these audits. 100% hip fracture form accuracy was not achieved [1370]. Radial head completeness stayed at 70% [1689], and the revision versus primary gap persisted [1635].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Only one audit here is on hip fracture data itself; the rest are joint registry and coding. Check a sample of your own entries against the notes, not just form completion. Coding audits show real money lost, £29,325 in one [1657], which gets management attention.
topic_knowledge.evidence: Detailed records in this library; judgement written by Claude from them

topic_knowledge.topic: Hip fracture care standards (national audit and best practice tariff)
topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Time to surgery is the hardest standard. Surgery within 36 hours was 39.6–48.3% [1535, 1491]; best practice tariff met in 28–44.4% [1535, 1526]. Orthogeriatric review is often late (mean 91 hours [1543]) or rare (11% [1766]). Delays are mainly for medical review or theatre space [1453, 1488]. Bone health and falls assessment lag.
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Whole pathway redesign with orthogeriatricians: surgery within 36 hours 39.6% to 84%, tariff 28% to 83%, 30-day mortality 7.8% to 5.3% [1535]. A joint admission pathway: mortality 14% to 4% [1543]. A clerking booklet and orthogeriatric rounds: tariff 44.4% to 91.7% [1526]. A national database with dashboards: geriatrician assessment 11% to 86% [1766].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Stopping continuous audit: surgery within 48 hours fell from 98.4% to 91.8% and ED waits worsened until it restarted [1519]. Benchmarking and teaching lifted nerve blocks only from 8.0% to 25.4% [1699]. Circulating results left function and mortality unchanged [1415]. National tariff compliance rose only 7% to 21% [1766].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: The national database already measures this every month; a local repeat adds little. Audit one breach cause, such as delay for medical review, or an unmeasured item like nerve block in ED. Gains fade when audit stops, so plan to keep measuring.
topic_knowledge.evidence: Detailed records in this library; judgement written by Claude from them

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: About half operated within 36 hours (41% [1132], 54% [1609]); mean time to theatre 43–53 hours, up to 80 hours in a major trauma centre [1184]. Commonest causes: no theatre space (28–51% of delays [1130][1490]) and anticoagulation. DOAC patients waited a median 39 h vs 25 h [1716].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Structural change. Two extra morning trauma lists: 41% to 78% within 36 h, mean 49 to 27 h [1132][1511]. Anaesthetic 'hot week': 54% to 87.5% within 36 h [1609]. Daytime emergency theatre: delays 49% to 26% [1130][1544]. Nurse-led IV vitamin K in ED: mean 53.71 to 37.61 h [1518].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Multicomponent bundle cut mean time from 80 to 55 h, but delays rose from 57.4% to 63.9% [1184]. Anaesthesia outreach sped consults but not surgery (within 48 h 38% to 51.6%, p=0.904) [1632]. INR sample education: rejection 16.5% to 11.1%, not significant [1737].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Heavily overdone, and the answer is always theatre capacity. Don't audit the overall time again. Audit a single cause instead: DOAC and warfarin pathways, rejected INR samples, or whether pre-op echo requests are appropriate [1750].
topic_knowledge.evidence: Detailed records in this library; judgement written by Claude from them

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Most miss the four-hour standard. Mean time to ward 417 minutes [1129] and 8 hrs 29 mins, with 26% within four hours [1148]. Fewer than 41% within four hours in another unit [1192]. Delays sit before X-ray and orthopaedic review.
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Multidisciplinary simulation on the pathway for 32 ED and related staff: 26% to 72% within four hours, mean 8 hrs 29 mins to 5 hrs 58 mins [1148]. A fast-track protocol: mean 2 h 45 min to 1 h 32 min, within one hour 3/104 to 24/90 [1405].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Early orthopaedic review before full workup cut time to ward only from 417 to 333 minutes, still well above four hours [1129].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Small topic with few audits. Measure where the time goes, step by step from arrival to X-ray, review and bed, rather than a single total time. Re-audit simulation gains after staff turnover, since no audit here shows they last.

topic_knowledge.topic: Index admission cholecystectomy for acute gallstone disease
topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Most units fall far short of cholecystectomy within 7–8 days: often 0–20% (0/61, 10%, 11%, 18.2%, 18.4%), a few 47–58.5%, and 75–87% in two. Waits after discharge run to months (68–125.8 days; 98.2 weeks). Readmission while waiting is common: 14–58%. Theatre capacity and ERCP/MRCP delays are the usual causes.
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: A full pathway with more ultrasound, a weekly theatre session and senior-led coding: 58% to 100% within 8 days [2227]. An e-referral system: wait 98.2 to 47.7 weeks [2186]. A referral proforma: pathway acceptance 10.5% to 29.2%, stay 6.45 to 3.88 days [2520]. Median admission to theatre 106.5 to 70.7 hours [2467].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Teaching and posters: within 7 days 75.3% to 68% [2336]. A hot gallbladder list and weekend list during COVID: hot gallbladder rate 8.8% to 10.8%, readmission 20.6% to 29.7% [2309]. A weekly hot list gave only 14% compliance [2122]. Opening the hot list to other surgeons left overall surgery at 21% [2389].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Overdone. Nearly every unit finds the same low rate and the same cause, theatre capacity. Don't repeat the timing audit. Measure readmissions and bed days while waiting, or coding accuracy (60% miscoded in one audit), to make the business case.
topic_knowledge.evidence: Detailed records in this library; judgement written by Claude from them

topic_knowledge.usual_baseline: Risk assessment on admission is usually done (93–100%) [1390][1702][2717]. The weak items are lying and standing BP, 25–34% [1610][1702][1903], and medication review after a fall, 9.09% [1817] and 22% [1761]. Call bell in reach 56% [1823]. Nationally, flat lifting equipment used in 22% [1169].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_works: Prompts built into routine. Education, SystmOne prompts and weekly MDT fall reviews: medication review 22% to 94% [1761]. Teaching, posters and aide-memoires: LSBP 32% to 83.3% [1610]. Huddle reminders and flyers: LSBP 34% to 68% [1702]. Stickers, teaching and handover reminders: call bell in reach 56% to 93.88% [1823]. Checklist and education: composite 65% to 90% [1903].
topic_knowledge.fix_that_fails: Continuous national audit moved slowly: flat lifting 22% to 29%, medical assessment within 30 minutes 52% to 60% [1169]. LSBP stayed at 65% after a checklist [1903]. LSBP was sometimes ticked as done when it was not [1702]. The call bell project showed no link with falls [1823].
topic_knowledge.consultant_advice: Lying and standing BP has been done often with the same result. More useful: audit medication review and deprescribing after a fall, which was 9.09% in one hospital [1817], or post-fall management such as CT head criteria [1171]. Measure falls or harm, not just process.
